extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing NIH/NIMH research grant applications, focusing on common mistakes across the scored review criteria and administrative requirements. Covers scientific review dimensions, human/animal subject protections, budgeting, and rigor/reproducibility expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too ambitious, too much work proposed; Unfocused aims, unclear goals; Limited aims and uncertain future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither significant nor exciting new research (i.e., will not advance science); Lack of compelling rationale; Incremental and low impact research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inadequate demonstration of expertise or publications in approaches; Low productivity, few recent papers; No collaborators recruited or no letters from collaborators; Need a more senior collaborator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not clearly addressed in application; Not innovative (i.e., new).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much unnecessary experimental detail; Not enough detail on approaches, especially untested ones; Not enough preliminary data to establish feasibility; Feasibility of each aim not shown; Little or no expertise with approach; Lack of appropriate controls; Not directly testing hypothesis; Correlative or descriptive data; Inadequate consideration of power; Experiments not directed towards mechanisms; No discussion of alternative models or hypotheses; No discussion of potential pitfalls; No discussion of interpretation of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Little demonstration of institutional support; Little or no necessary equipment; Little evidence of effective collaboration among institutions, if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (considered but not individually scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other review criteria that are not scored individually but are considered in the overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protections for Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women, Minorities, & Children; Vertebrate Animals; Biohazards; Resubmission; Renewal; Revision. Applicants should refer to the Instruction Guides for these scored and non-scored criteria (SF424 (R&R), PHS 398).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Human or Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems with the description of Human or Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must properly describe protections for human subjects and vertebrate animals; see 'Research Involving Human Subjects' and related inclusion guidance links for details and specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to use the required modular budget format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modular budgets are applicable to certain research grant applications requesting $250,000 or less per year for direct costs. Note: sub-award/consortium F&A costs are not factored into the direct cost limit. Consortium F&A costs may be requested in addition to the $250,000 limit. The modular budget is applicable only to applications for R01, R03, R15, R21, and R34 and their corresponding cooperative agreement activity codes. Guidance is available in Section 5.4 of the application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-award/consortium budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to include separate sub-award/consortium budgets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete sub-award/consortium budget form (including the budget justification section) should be completed by each consortium grantee organization. Foreign grantee applications must only include detailed (non-modular) budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the budget justification to provide the additional information requested in each budget category identified in Section 4.7 of the application directions, along with other information the applicant wishes to submit to support the budget request. The following budget categories always must be justified, where applicable: equipment, travel, participant/trainee support, and other direct cost categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of significant budget changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to explain significant changes from the initial year budget
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a justification for any significant increases or decreases from the initial year budget. Justify budgets with more than a standard escalation from the initial to the future year(s) of support. Also use this section to explain any exclusion applied to the F&A base calculation. Though an organization may ask for any escalation factor it wishes, NIMH may award only up to the set amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: New instructions and revised review criteria (effective for applications submitted Jan 26, 2016 and beyond) focus on enhancing rigor and transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and applicants should address: (1) the scientific premise of the proposed research, (2) rigorous experimental design for robust and unbiased results, (3) consideration of relevant biological variables, and (4) authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources.
